html:
Starting a Community Care Facility (CCF) for adults with developmental disabilities in California allows you to provide essential residential support to one of the state’s most underserved populations. With approximately 481,601 individuals awaiting services and $13.6 billion in annual DDS funding, the opportunity is significant. This guide covers everything you need to know about licensing and launching your program.

Understanding California DD Residential Regulations

California’s residential services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) operate under a complex regulatory framework involving multiple state agencies.

Regulatory Framework

California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD) licenses Community Care Facilities, which include:

  • Adult Residential Facilities (ARF)
  • Group Homes
  • Small Family Homes

California Department of Developmental Services (DDS) oversees the Regional Center system, which:

  • Coordinates services for individuals with I/DD
  • Authorizes and funds residential placements
  • Establishes rate and service level requirements

Key regulatory elements include:

  • CCLD Licensure: Required for all residential facilities
  • Regional Center Vendorization: Required for DDS funding
  • HCBS Compliance: Federal Home and Community-Based Services requirements
  • Service Levels: Tiered system based on resident support needs
  • Background Checks: Required for all staff and household members

Understanding both licensing and vendorization processes is essential for success.

Facility Types and Service Levels

California offers various residential models for adults with developmental disabilities. Understanding these options helps you design an appropriate program.

Facility Types

Adult Residential Facilities (ARF):

  • Serves adults with I/DD in home-like settings
  • Typically 4-6 residents
  • Most common CCF type for DD population

Small Family Homes:

  • Owner/operator lives in home
  • Maximum 6 residents
  • Most integrated, home-like option

Group Homes:

  • Licensed for 7+ residents
  • More structured programming
  • May specialize in higher-needs populations

Service Levels

California is implementing new service levels:

  • Level 1: Minimal support needs
  • Level 2: Moderate support
  • Level 3: Enhanced support
  • Level 4: Intensive support (new)
  • Level 5: Medical/behavioral complexity (new)

Higher service levels receive higher reimbursement but require enhanced staffing and programming.

Specialty Programs

High-demand specializations include:

  • Behavioral support services
  • Medically complex care
  • Traumatic brain injury
  • Dual diagnosis (I/DD + mental health)
  • Transition-age youth (18-22)

Licensing Requirements and Application Process

Obtaining California CCF licensure requires coordination between CCLD licensing and Regional Center vendorization.

CCLD Licensing Process

  • Pre-Application:
  • Attend orientation
  • Identify facility location
  • Confirm zoning compliance
  • Obtain fire clearance
  • Application Submission:
  • Complete LIC 200 series forms
  • Pay application fees
  • Submit facility plans
  • Provide ownership documentation
  • Background Checks:
  • Criminal record clearances
  • Child abuse index check
  • DMV record (if transporting)
  • Facility Approval:
  • Fire clearance
  • Health department clearance
  • Building inspection
  • Facility evaluation visit
  • License Issuance:
  • Initial license (may be provisional)
  • Capacity and population specified
  • Annual renewal required

Regional Center Vendorization

After CCLD licensing:

  • Application: Submit vendorization application to local Regional Center
  • Program Design: Describe services, staffing, programming
  • Rate Determination: Service level and rate negotiation
  • Contract Execution: Vendor contract with Regional Center
  • Referral Process: Begin receiving resident referrals

Developing Your Business Plan

A comprehensive business plan guides your facility’s development. California’s DD residential market has unique dynamics your plan should address.

Market Analysis

Research your service area:

  • Regional Center Service Area: Each of 21 Regional Centers has distinct needs
  • Population Needs: Individuals awaiting placement, aging out of family homes
  • Competition: Existing vendors, capacity, specializations
  • Unmet Needs: High-acuity populations, geographic gaps
  • Referral Patterns: Regional Center placement priorities

Financial Projections

Develop realistic forecasts:

  • Startup Costs: Facility, modifications, licensing, equipment ($200,000-$500,000)
  • Operating Costs: Staffing (60-70%), facility, supplies, administration
  • Revenue Model: Regional Center reimbursement based on service level
  • Break-Even Analysis: Typically 12-24 months at 70-80% occupancy

Reimbursement Understanding

Know your revenue structure:

  • Per Diem Rates: Based on service level assignment
  • Personal and Incidental: $168/month per resident
  • Enhanced Rates: For Level 4 and 5 services
  • Supplemental Funding: Specialized services, behavioral supports

Facility Requirements and Design

CCF facilities must meet CCLD standards while creating home-like environments that support resident independence and community integration.

Physical Environment

  • Residential Character: Home-like appearance required
  • Neighborhood Integration: Consistent with community
  • Accessibility: Full ADA compliance
  • Privacy: Personal space for each resident
  • Community Access: Location supporting integration

Space Requirements

  • Adequate bedroom space (private or semi-private)
  • Common living areas
  • Dining space
  • Kitchen access
  • Bathroom ratios per Title 22
  • Outdoor space
  • Staff areas

HCBS Settings Requirements

Federal requirements emphasize:

  • Private units preferred
  • Lockable doors
  • Choice and control
  • Community access
  • Visitor policies
  • Lease/residency agreements

Safety Features

  • Fire safety systems
  • Emergency egress
  • Secure medication storage
  • Hazard-free environment
  • Emergency communication

Staffing Requirements and Training

CCFs require adequate staffing to provide 24-hour supervision and support. Staffing levels vary by service level and resident needs.

Required Personnel

Administrator:

  • Facility management
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Staff supervision
  • Regional Center coordination

Direct Support Professionals (DSP):

  • Personal care assistance
  • Daily living support
  • Activity facilitation
  • Transportation

Staffing Ratios

Staffing requirements vary by:

  • Service level designation
  • Individual resident needs
  • Time of day (awake vs. sleep)
  • Programming requirements

Training Requirements

Initial Training:

  • 35 hours pre-service training
  • First aid and CPR
  • Medication administration
  • Behavior management basics
  • Individual rights

Ongoing Training:

  • 20 hours annual training
  • Topic-specific requirements
  • Competency verification
  • Professional development

DSP Workforce

Address workforce challenges:

  • Competitive wages
  • Benefits and incentives
  • Career development paths
  • Positive work culture
  • Training investments

Policies and Procedures Development

Comprehensive policies demonstrate your commitment to quality care and regulatory compliance.

Resident Rights Policies

California emphasizes individual rights:

  • Choice and self-determination
  • Privacy and dignity
  • Personal relationships
  • Financial management
  • Community integration
  • Grievance procedures

Care Policies

Individual Program Plans:

  • Person-centered planning
  • Goal development
  • Progress monitoring
  • Annual updates

Daily Operations:

  • Medication management
  • Health monitoring
  • Behavioral support
  • Personal care
  • Activities and programming

Health and Safety

  • Emergency procedures
  • Incident reporting
  • Infection control
  • Abuse prevention
  • Disaster preparedness

Administrative Policies

  • Personnel practices
  • Record keeping
  • Confidentiality
  • Quality assurance
  • Financial management

Marketing and Referral Development

Building census in a CCF requires strong relationships with Regional Centers and the service system.

Regional Center Relationships

Your primary referral source:

  • Build relationships with service coordinators
  • Demonstrate quality outcomes
  • Participate in vendor meetings
  • Respond promptly to referrals
  • Communicate effectively about residents

Person-Centered Approach

Successful placements require:

  • Thorough pre-admission assessments
  • Good match between resident and home
  • Transition planning and support
  • Family engagement
  • Ongoing communication

Reputation Building

  • Quality services and outcomes
  • Regulatory compliance record
  • Staff stability and expertise
  • Family satisfaction
  • Community integration success

Compliance and Quality Assurance

Maintaining regulatory compliance and high-quality services requires systematic monitoring and improvement.

Dual Compliance

Monitor both systems:

  • CCLD licensing requirements
  • Regional Center contract requirements
  • HCBS settings compliance
  • Individual plan compliance

Quality Assurance

Implement comprehensive monitoring:

  • Individual outcome tracking
  • Incident trend analysis
  • Satisfaction surveys
  • Staff performance monitoring
  • Program effectiveness evaluation

Regulatory Compliance

Maintain ongoing compliance:

  • Annual licensing renewal
  • Inspection preparedness
  • Staff credential maintenance
  • Training documentation
  • Record keeping excellence

Continuous Improvement

  • Self-assessment processes
  • Quality improvement plans
  • Best practice implementation
  • Staff development
  • Outcome focus

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to get licensed and vendored?

CCLD licensing takes 3-6 months. Regional Center vendorization adds 2-4 months after licensure.

What is the cost to start a CCF for adults with DD?

Startup costs typically range from $200,000 to $500,000 depending on facility acquisition/modification and capacity.

What are typical reimbursement rates?

Rates vary by service level, ranging from approximately $150-$350+ per day depending on resident needs and service level.

How do I get referrals from the Regional Center?

Build relationships with service coordinators, demonstrate quality services, and maintain good communication. Specialization in underserved populations helps.

Can I serve other populations in my facility?

ARF licenses allow serving adults with various disabilities. Vendorization specifies the population you serve. Focus on one population initially.

What service levels should I target?

Consider your expertise and facilities. Levels 4 and 5 provide higher reimbursement but require enhanced staffing and capabilities.
